Synopsis
Mamaearth has closed a $50 million funding round led by Belgian investment fund Sofina , valuing the direct-to-consumer ( D2C ) personal care brand at $730 million, one of the most valued new-age D2C brands in the country.
Existing investor Sequoia Capital also participated in the round, while early investors Fireside Ventures, Stellaris Venture Partners, Sharp Ventures and Titan Capital sold some stakes in a secondary transaction, the company said.
In a secondary share sale, the money does not flow into the company directly but goes to investors selling their stakes.
The latest fundraising round was mostly in the form of primary capital infusion, while there was also a share buyback from some of its early employees.
ET was the first to report on May 13 that Sofina was looking to lead Mamaearth’s new funding round. Sofina had picked up a small stake in Mamaearth through a secondary share sale, ET reported, but it was not announced formally.
Sources said the company was last valued at $200-$300 million.
After a round of primary capital raising in early 2020, Mamaearth’s valuation was pegged at around $100 million but that increased gradually during secondary share sales over the past few months. Mamaearth cofounder and chief executive Varun Alagh declined to share details of the secondary share sales.
Mamaearth will use the fresh capital to double down on its brand’s growth through deeper offline expansion and also explore acquisitions in the beauty and personal care space, Alagh told ET.
“The Mamaearth team is constantly pushing the boundaries in the personal care space through their disruptive innovations, rapid execution pace and focus on delighting customers,” said Yana Kachurina, investment manager, Sofina Ventures SA.
Rise of D2C Alagh said Mamaearth's own online platform is its single largest channel of total sales, without giving specific numbers.
According to Jefferies, Mamaearth’s D2C platform generates 35% of total sales while offline channels account for 20%.
“This round will help amplify the process and strengthen the D2C and offline expansion of Mamaearth, along with further accelerating the growth of The Derma Co which is already showing early signs of success, since its launch in 2020,” he said.
Derma Co is a separate skincare brand from Mamaearth parent Honasa Consumer.
It has over 140 products under the Mamaearth brand and around 40 products under The Derma Co. The offline channel's contribution to the company's total sales would go up once the expansion is completed.

Image for Mamaearth parent raises $52 million in funding led by Sequoia Global ETtech Illustration: Rahul Awasthi
New Delhi: Honasa Consumer , the owner of the Mamaearth brand has raised $52 million in a latest round of funding led by Sequoia Global at a valuation of $1.15 billion, making it the latest to join the unicorn club .
The round also saw participation from some existing investors like Belgian Sofina Ventures SA and some new funds such as UAE-based Evolvence, said Varun Alagh , cofounder and CEO, Honasa Consumer.
Some early investors like Fireside Ventures and Stellaris partially exited in this round. There was also a share buyback from some of its employees.
Other existing investors include Some of its existing investors include Sequoia Capital, Sharrp Ventures and Titan Capital.
“Seqouia Global, Sofina and Evolvence have unique strengths in US, Europe & GCC, respectively, which will help us grow internationally and learn from others in these markets," said Alagh.
The company which aims to touch a revenue figure of $1 billion in the next five years will deploy the funds towards expanding its portfolio of personal care D2C brands. Honasa Consumer owns three brands – Mamaearth, The Derma Co, and Aqualogica, launched a few weeks ago, and will introduce more brands in the coming months.
Along with launching new brands, Honasa will continue aggressively expanding distribution for existing brands -Mamaearth and The Derma Co. and explore strategic inorganic growth opportunities in the beauty and personal care segment.
It plans to expand the outlets to the top 20 cities where the sale is highest. Alagh said Mamaearth's own online platform is its single largest channel of total sales, without giving specific numbers. The products are also available on online marketplaces like Amazon, Flipkart and Nykaa. It currently caters to over 1000 cities in India.

New Update
mamaearth
Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, has announced the resignation of its Chief Business Officer Yatish Bhargava, less than a year after appointing him to the role.
According to a stock exchange filing on Friday, Bhargava has resigned due to “personal circumstances” and will cease to be part of the company’s senior management with effect from the close of business hours on May 15, 2026.
Bhargava had joined the Gurugram-based company in June last year after the position remained vacant since February 28, following the resignation of Zairus Master, who had also stepped down citing personal reasons.
At the time of his appointment, Honasa had designated Bhargava as Chief Business Officer and Senior Management Personnel with immediate effect.
Bhargava brought over 17 years of experience in P&L management and leading large-scale teams across general trade, modern trade, and e-commerce.
Prior to joining Honasa, he held senior leadership roles at Flipkart and Hindustan Unilever Limited.
On the financial front, Honasa reported a 16.2% year-on-year increase in operating revenue to Rs 602 crore in Q3 FY26, compared to Rs 518 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
The company’s profit after tax nearly doubled to Rs 50 crore during the quarter from Rs 26 crore in Q3 FY25.
The company has also guided for revenue growth in the late twenties for Q4 FY26, the results for which are yet to be filed.
According to Honasa, its flagship brand Mamaearth is expected to report growth in the teens during the quarter, while newer brands including The Derma Co., Aqualogica, BBlunt, Dr. Sheth’s, Staze, and Lumineve are likely to outperform with growth in the mid-twenties range.

Mamaearth parent posts Rs 756 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; doubles profit
Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, announced its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027 (Q1 FY27).
[](https://www.linkedin.com/sharing/share-offsite/?url=https://entrackr.com/fintrackr/mamaearth-parent-posts-rs-756-cr-revenue-in-q1-fy27-doubles-profit-12257228&title=Mamaearth parent posts Rs 756 Cr revenue in Q1 FY27; doubles profit)
New Update
mamaearth
Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, announced its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027 (Q1 FY27). The company reported a 27% year-on-year growth in its scale during the quarter, while its profit more than doubled to Rs 90 crore, its highest quarterly profit to date.
The company’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 756 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 595 crore in Q1 FY26, according to its financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE).
Mamaearth Q1FY27
The company did not provide a detailed revenue breakdown, it also recorded Rs 22.5 crore from non-operating activities, taking its overall revenue to Rs 778 crore in Q1 FY27 during the quarter.
According to its shareholders’ letter, Honasa’s recent acquisition, men’s grooming brand Reginald Men, has grown more than 2X since the acquisition and now has an annual revenue run rate of over Rs 150 crore, the company said.
For the D2C brand, cost of materials remained the largest cost centre and rose 34% year-on-year to Rs 229 crore from Rs 171 crore. Employee benefit expenses increased 10% to Rs 66 crore from Rs 60 crore.
Finance costs, depreciation and amortization expenses and other overhead drove Honasa’s overall expenses to Rs 659 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 564 crore in the year-ago quarter.
At the bottom line, the company reported a more than 2X jump in profit to Rs 90.45 crore in Q1 FY27 from Rs 41.33 crore in Q1 FY26.
EBITDA also doubled to Rs 110 crore during the quarter, with an EBITDA margin of 14%.
On a sequential basis, revenue from operations increased 15.% from Rs 657 crore in Q4 FY26 , while profit rose 30.3% from Rs 69.44 crore.
Mamaearth closed Thursday’s trading session at Rs 479.45 per share, giving the company a market capitalisation of around Rs 15,255 crore.
In June 2026, Mamaearth parent Honasa Consumer acquired a 58% stake in nutraceuticals company Fluence Pharma at an enterprise value of around Rs 135 crore.

Review: Mamaearth Ubtan Face Wash
Pallavi
*
Hey friends,
I am back with a detailed face wash review for you all. And the product that I am going to talk about today is the popular and much in demand Mamaearth Ubtan Face Wash with Turmeric & Saffron .
Mamaearth Ubtan Face Wash was on my wish list for quite some time now because of a few attractions.
Firstly, it claims to pamper the skin by rejuvenating dull, tanned skin and making it look fresh and bright. Secondly, the age-old tradition of using 'ubtan' as a beauty treatment for skin brightening has been included in this face wash. In addition to this, Mamaearth is the first & I think the only Made Safe Certified Indian brand .
Well, keep reading to know more about it & how this face wash fared on my sometimes dry-combination skin type.
About Mamaearth Ubtan Face Wash
Externally, Mamaearth Ubtan Face wash has a striking look with white, green, brown and yellowish-orange colors primarily coming into play on their plastic tube packaging.
For example, apart from the name - Mamaearth Ubtan Face Wash with Turmeric & Saffron, details like ' for tan removal ', its net volume and it being ' paraben & SLS free ', ' hypoallergenic ' and 'suits all skin types' are given at the front side.
* Mamaearth Ubtan Face Wash (Buy it here)
Ingredients
Hero Ingredients (Found on Mamaearth website)
* Saffron: Saffron has many vitamins and antioxidants that are beneficial to the skin. They not only add radiance to the skin but also soothe it.
* Turmeric: Turmeric protects the skin from free radical damage due to its natural anti-inflammatory and anti-septic properties.
Claims & Features
Mamearth Ubtan Face Wash has a colorful and sturdy packaging, which is attractive to look at. It is also hygienic and travel-friendly, since the actual product, i.e., the face wash, doesn't spill due to its slightly thick and creamy texture .
In fact the face wash, looks similar to an ubtan paste - yellowish in color with tiny dark brown granules in it.
The fragrance of Mamaearth Ubtan Face Wash is pleasant but fades away after washing. However, I could smell turmeric in it. This smell is not strong, so people with sensitive noses can use it comfortably.
On the other hand, Mamaearth Ubtan Face Wash does offer a few benefits. For example, it is free from paraben and SLS, provides light exfoliation, gives an instant brightness to the skin, and does not dry it out.
So, here I conclude my review of Mamaearth Ubtan Face Wash with Turmeric and Saffron. What do you think of it, friends? Have any of you tried it? If yes, then I would love to read about your experience in the comments section below. 🤗
